hints.title: Count Frequencies
hints.text: Count occurrences of each number. Removing a number eliminates all its instances at once.

hints.title: Greedy Largest Frequencies
hints.text: To minimize the set size, always choose to eliminate the number with the largest remaining frequency.

hints.title: Cumulative Removal Check
hints.text: Sort frequencies descending. Accumulate removed elements until total removed >= len(arr) // 2.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from collections import Counter

class Solution:
    def minSetSize(self, arr: list[int]) -> int:
        counts = Counter(arr)
        freqs = sorted(counts.values(), reverse=True)
        removed = 0
        needed = (len(arr) + 1) // 2
        ans = 0
        for f in freqs:
            removed += f
            ans += 1
            if removed >= needed:
                break
        return ans
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Removing arbitrary elements without prioritizing largest frequencies leads to larger set sizes.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Counting frequencies and sorting descending allows greedy threshold attainment in linearithmic time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate applies greedy removal by largest frequencies first.
complexity.notes: Can achieve O(N) using bucket sort on frequencies since max frequency is N.
